input.title: Animate auto height (GSAP demo)
input.technique: Measure-then-tween. CSS cannot transition `height: auto`, so the canonical GSAP recipe is: (1) read the natural pixel height of the content with `el.scrollHeight` (or `getBoundingClientRect().height` after temporarily setting `height: auto`), (2) tween from `height: 0` (or any starting px value) to that measured pixel value, (3) on completion, set `height: "auto"` so the element continues to respond to content changes after the animation. The Flip plugin can do the same thing more declaratively (`Flip.getState` -> change to `auto` -> `Flip.from(state, {...})`), but the lightweight measure-then-tween approach does NOT require Flip and is what the official GSAP "animate auto height" demo is built around.
input.keyMechanic: The trick is that GSAP can tween any numeric value, so you simply convert "auto" into a concrete pixel target by reading `scrollHeight` before the tween starts, then animate to that number. The crucial final step is `onComplete: () => gsap.set(el, { height: "auto" })` — without it, the panel stays locked at the measured pixel height and breaks if the content later reflows (e.g. viewport resize, font load, nested expand). For a two-way open/close you typically build a paused timeline so you can `.play()` / `.reverse()` and you re-measure on every open in case content changed.
input.a11yNotes: Set `overflow: hidden` only during the tween — leaving it on can clip focus rings and tooltips. Add `aria-hidden={!open}` (or better, also toggle `inert` on the collapsed panel) so screen readers and keyboard tab order skip hidden content. Pair the trigger with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the panel's id. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`: wrap the tween in `gsap.matchMedia()` and use `duration: 0` (or a `gsap.set`) when the user prefers reduced motion. Avoid animating height on elements that contain focusable inputs unless you also manage focus, otherwise focus can land in a 0-height region.
